rulings.challenge_claim: LF (high, challenge): the row defends only the right boundary against 25:10 and leaves an equally live left-seam catchword chain with 25:8 undisclosed (shared root ר-י-ב and the exact word רֵעֶ֑ךָ). OL (support): 25:9's paired imperatives form a complete instruction distinct from 25:10's dependent pen-clause, contrasted with the genuine kaf...ken dependency at 26:18-19.
rulings.grounds: byte tier (verse_map_oshb.json, independently re-split): oshb:Prov.25.8 carries לָרִ֗ב (root ר-י-ב, 'to go out to dispute') and closes on רֵעֶֽךָ ('your neighbor'); oshb:Prov.25.9 opens with the cognate noun-plus-verb construction רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב (same root) and repeats רֵעֶ֑ךָ — a byte-true root-plus-exact-word chain straddling the row's own left seam, confirmed absent from oshb:Prov.25.10 (no ר-י-ב or רעך token there), so the standing cross-seam-cohesion disclosure rule is triggered and was not met. Independently confirmed the same writer pass already names a weaker, non-adjacent '25:8-9' echo inside P11-013's own rejected_alternative, showing the method was available but not applied to this row's own immediate seam -- LF's high challenge upheld. OL's contrast citation is independently byte-confirmed: oshb:Prov.26.18 opens כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ (kaf-prefixed comparative) and oshb:Prov.26.19 opens כֵּֽן (the apodosis particle) -- a genuine marked simile frame, correctly distinguishing 25:9-10 (unmarked) from a true dependency. This is a distinct question from LF's disclosure point (right-boundary soundness vs. left-seam disclosure), not the same defect -- both stand.
rulings.remedy: Add disclosure of the left-seam catchword chain with 25:8 (root ר-י-ב plus exact word רֵעֶ֑ךָ) to the row's rationale / boundary_evidence_refs as tier-appropriate texture, not a boundary driver (matching the parity already given the weaker 25:8-9 mention in P11-013). Cure test: check_refs_mirror.py must show 25:8 disclosed in P11-006's own boundary_evidence_refs; the disclosure must not alter unit_type (single_proverb stands -- no merge is warranted).

rulings.challenge_claim: Both LF and OL: the row's claim that the shared זהב token 'occurs nowhere else in this part' is a false exclusivity digit; the token also occurs at 27:21, inside P11.
rulings.grounds: skeleton tier, sweep.py --skel זהב independently rerun: 7 verses book-wide (Prov.11.22, Prov.17.3, Prov.20.15, Prov.22.1, Prov.25.11, Prov.25.12, Prov.27.21), of which 3 fall inside P11 (25.1-27.27): Prov.25.11, Prov.25.12, Prov.27.21 -- confirmed against oshb:Prov.27.21 (מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ לְפִ֣י מַהֲלָלֽוֹ). 'Nowhere else in this part' is false; the correct digit is 3 part-internal verses, not 2. Both primaries independently reached the same digit and the same corrected phrasing (the row's own rejected_alternative's narrower 'nowhere else ADJACENT in the part' survives the sweep) -- same defect from both sources, consolidated into one ruling.
rulings.remedy: Correct the rationale / observed_substrate_signals from 'occurs nowhere else in this part' to the digit-bearing corrected claim (occurs at 3 part-internal verses: 25:11, 25:12, 27:21; the pair's adjacency-plus-exact-repetition, not part-wide exclusivity, is what argues clustering). Cure test: sweep.py --skel זהב count/refs must match the row's revised digit; check_universals.py must no longer flag an unqualified exclusivity claim on this row.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both LF and OL: the row's claim that a skeleton sweep of 25:17 against its neighbors 'comes back empty' is false -- 25:16 and 25:17 share the root ש-ב-ע inside a matching פן-clause warning frame. OL additionally flags zero Hebrew bytes quoted anywhere in the row.
rulings.grounds: skeleton tier, sweep.py --skel שבע independently rerun: 25 verses book-wide, including the consecutive pair oshb:Prov.25.16 (תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ) and oshb:Prov.25.17 (יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗) -- the same root inside each verse's own pen-clause slot. The row's 'comes back empty' claim is the direct opposite of the tool's output. Because ש-ב-ע recurs in 25 verses book-wide (a common root, not bounded), it does not clear the C5 catchword-cluster bar, so single_proverb likely still holds -- but the absence claim must be corrected to a root-commonality disclosure rather than an (incorrect) negative-sweep claim. Independently confirmed: the row's rationale, rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals, and device_notes contain zero quoted Hebrew bytes anywhere, unlike sibling rows in this cluster (e.g. P11-006, P11-017) that do quote bytes -- OL's secondary point holds. Same core defect (false absence claim) from both sources; OL's Hebrew-quotation point is a compounding sub-finding on the same row, not a distinct defect.
rulings.remedy: Replace 'the skeleton sweep against both neighbors comes back empty' with an accurate root-commonality disclosure naming the shared ש-ב-ע root at 25:16/25:17 and the book-wide count that keeps it below the cluster bar; add at least one quoted Hebrew byte span per the standing original-language-quotation rule. Cure test: sweep.py --skel שבע rerun must match the corrected digit cited in the row; the row must carry >=1 collate.py byte-tier-verified Hebrew quote.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL (medium, challenge): the 'likened to' / simile device label for 25:19 rests on the WEB gloss; the Hebrew carries no kaf/ken comparative marking. (LF supported a distinct claim on this row: the 25:19/25:20 ביום overlap is correctly treated as non-bounded texture.)
rulings.grounds: byte tier: oshb:Prov.25.19 (שֵׁ֣ן רֹ֭עָה וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרָֽה) independently confirmed to carry no kaf-prefix or כן-apodosis anywhere -- unmarked nominal juxtaposition (three images set beside each other), not a marked simile. The row's rationale ('is likened to') and device_notes ('Synthetic simile') both derive the device label from the WEB rendering rather than the Hebrew construction, contrary to the standing rule requiring the original language be quoted for every boundary-relevant original-language claim. LF's support verdict addressed a separate, valid question (the ביום collocation with 25:20 correctly treated as book-wide texture, not bounded cohesion) which is independently confirmed accurate and unaffected by this defect -- distinct issues on the same row, not the same defect.
rulings.remedy: Replace 'likened to' / 'simile' language in rationale and device_notes with construction-accurate wording (unmarked nominal juxtaposition -- no kaf/ken particle at 25:19); stop citing the WEB 'is like' gloss as device evidence. The existing ביום-texture argument needs no change. Cure test: collate.py --ref oshb:Prov.25.19 must show no kaf/ken bytes cited in support of any simile relabeling.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF (low, challenge): the rejected_alternative's parenthetical '(see that row)' is a positional cross-row reference rather than verse-anchored, a register-purge violation even though 25:19 is already named in the same clause.
rulings.grounds: Row text (draft_rows_combined.jsonl, P11-016 rejected_alternative) independently confirmed to read: "No merge with 25:19 (see that row) or 25:21 ... was warranted." '(see that row)' names the corpus artifact positionally, not the text, violating the standing register-purge rule (no positional row references in row prose ever; cross-row references are verse-anchored). Purely a hygiene defect -- substantive content (the boundary calls against 25:19 and 25:21, and the PE disclosure at 25:20) is independently confirmed sound.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the rejected_alternative to drop '(see that row)', keeping only the verse citation, e.g. 'No merge with 25:19 or 25:21 was warranted.' Cure test: a register-purge check of the row's prose for positional / file-structure phrases ('see that row', 'as above', decision-ids, etc.) must return zero hits.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL (high, challenge): the 'double simile' claim for 25:20 is argued entirely from the WEB translation; the row quotes zero Hebrew bytes, and its only observed_substrate_signals entry is a web: tag standing in for Hebrew evidence.
rulings.grounds: byte tier: oshb:Prov.25.20 (מַ֥עֲדֶה בֶּ֨גֶד בְּי֣וֹם קָ֭רָה חֹ֣מֶץ עַל נָ֑תֶר וְשָׁ֥ר בַּ֝שִּׁרִ֗ים עַ֣ל לֶב רָֽע) independently confirmed to carry no kaf or כן anywhere across its three juxtaposed clauses. The row's rationale and its sole observed_substrate_signals entry ('web: Prov.25.20 double simile complete within the verse') both rest the device claim on the WEB 'As...so is' rendering rather than Hebrew bytes -- a compounding violation (both the rationale field AND the mandatory substrate-signal field lack Hebrew grounding), which is more severe than P11-015's single-field version of the same problem since observed_substrate_signals is meant to record substrate (Hebrew) signals specifically. High severity is warranted on that basis. The petuchah disclosure at 25:20 (pmarks_Prov.json: PE, single-witness) is independently confirmed correct and is unaffected by this defect.
rulings.remedy: Replace the observed_substrate_signals web: tag with a Hebrew-grounded (oshb:) signal, or relabel the device from 'double simile' to an unmarked-juxtaposition/imagery label consistent with the absence of kaf/ken at 25:20; if 'simile' language is retained it must quote Hebrew bytes, not the WEB rendering alone. Cure test: collate.py --ref oshb:Prov.25.20 confirms no kaf/ken bytes; observed_substrate_signals must not contain a bare web: tag standing in for a Hebrew substrate claim.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL (medium, challenge): the observed_substrate_signals claim that the closing phrase כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ is 'byte-identical across the pair' overclaims; the opening word (כְּ֭סִיל vs כְ֭סִיל) carries a dagesh in 26:4 absent in 26:5. (LF's support verdict called the same phrase 'byte-confirmed against source' without qualification.)
rulings.grounds: codepoint-level comparison independently run against verse_map_oshb.json confirms: the second word of the phrase, כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ, is byte-identical between oshb:Prov.26.4 and oshb:Prov.26.5 (exact codepoint match); the first word differs -- oshb:Prov.26.4's כְּ֭סִיל carries HEBREW POINT DAGESH OR MAPIQ (U+05BC) immediately after the initial kaf, absent from oshb:Prov.26.5's כְ֭סִיל. 'Byte-identical across the pair' is false as stated for the phrase as a whole (one of two words differs by a point), per the standing tier/ordinal discipline requiring exact tier-matched language. LF's support call ('byte-confirmed against source') is the imprecise reading OL's challenge corrects. The core reversed-imperative argument (אַל תַּ֣עַן in 26:4 vs עֲנֵ֣ה in 26:5) is unaffected and remains byte-sound.
rulings.remedy: Correct 'byte-identical across the pair' to name which word is exactly byte-identical (כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ, collate.py-confirmed) and which carries a point variant (the kesil token, dagesh present in 26:4 / absent in 26:5). Cure test: collate.py byte-tier diff of both kesil tokens must be reflected accurately in the row's language; the reversed-imperative argument itself needs no change.
